title: SLO guardrail fallback playbook - circuit-breaker profiling and restore validation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an operational playbook that links SLO guardrails to automated fallback actions, with focused circuit-breaker threshold profiling and end-to-end backup/restore validation for active-passive failovers. The goal is to ensure low-latency inferencing paths can be safely degraded and recovered while meeting SLOs for critical routes and minimizing RTO/RPO under scheduled failover drills.
background: We have recurring incidents where latency spikes on generation endpoints cascade into request queues and cause customer-visible SLO violations. Current circuit-breakers are conservative and rarely exercised in controlled conditions. Backups are taken regularly, but we've had uncertainty about state drift for ephemeral caches and session tokens after passive->active promotions. This ticket scopes a combined profiling and validation effort to make guardrail actions deterministic and tested.
playbook_steps: Inventory critical routes and map their SLO targets (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability).
Define guardrail thresholds per route: soft-alert, hard-alert, pre-fallback, fallback. Document in Console SLO dashboard.
Design circuit-breaker modes: monitor-only, soft-open (reject heavy ops), hard-open (reject all non-essential ops).
Implement profiling harness: run controlled load patterns (bursty, long-tail prompts, KV-heavy sessions) against candidate thresholds to capture latency, queue depth, and tail latencies.

Create a staged fallback script: 1) scale down model size on routing layer, 2) enable prefix-KV caching for warmed keys, 3) route a percentage to standby region. Support progressive canary (0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%).
Integrate guardrail triggers with rollout controller: automatic canary abort criteria (SLO regressions, error-rate spike, saturation).
Add a restore validation subroutine run post-passive-promotion: validate KV cache reconciliation, session token mapping, embedding index consistency, and sample-generation verification.
Document rollback actions and verification checks for each stage.
Schedule and run a cross-team drill (SRE, Runtime, Console, Solutions) and capture metrics and postmortem.
checklist: SLO mapping completed for all critical routes
Profiling harness (benchmarks + scenarios) checked into infra/tools
Fallback scripts in repository with idempotent retries
Canary orchestration wired to rollout controller
Restore validation tests integrated into recovery pipeline
Runbook page published in Confluence with contact on-call list
Drill scheduled and invite sent to stakeholders
test_scenarios: Burst spike: 10x traffic for 30s then drop back - verify soft-open behavior and queue shedding preserves p95 <= SLO.
Slow drift: gradual increase in p95 over 15m - validate system triggers soft-alert then executes canary routing at pre-fallback threshold.
Standby promotion: simulate network partition to primary region, execute passive->active promotion, run restore validation checks against sample user sessions.
KV inconsistency injection: write divergent state in standby cache and ensure validation detects reconciliation failures and aborts traffic cutover.
Fallback rollback: intentionally fail a canary at 5% and validate automatic rollback and blameless alerting flow.
rollback_plan: If any canary stage exceeds abort criteria (p95 regression > 15% vs baseline OR error-rate > 3x baseline OR saturation on target queues), immediately revert routing to previous stable variant, scale down temporary caches, and open a fast-track incident with SRE and Runtime leads. Execute restore verification in read-only mode and avoid writes until reconciliation is confirmed. Document timeline in drill notes.
acceptance_criteria: Automatic guardrail triggers fire in profiling harness and result in expected simulated fallback with no manual intervention
Canary orchestration successfully aborts when abort criteria met in at least three different test scenarios
Post-promotion restore validation passes for session reconciliation and embedding index consistency within the RPO target
Runbook is reviewed and approved by Platform Reliability and Runtime team
Drill completed with playbook steps executed and a follow-up action list created

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positive guardrail triggers could cause unnecessary rollbacks - Mitigation: require two independent signals (latency AND queue depth) before hard-open.
Risk: State drift in caches leading to inconsistent responses - Mitigation: read-only validation sweep and sample-user-generation comparisons before accepting traffic.
Risk: Canary rollback could cascade if rollback actions are not idempotent - Mitigation: ensure fallback scripts are idempotent and add fence tokens to avoid double-apply.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive shedding reduces customer value but protects SLOs; we decided on progressive degradation to balance availability and correctness.
Ops note: coordinate with Sales/Support for customer-facing messaging during drill windows.
Follow-up task: instrument token/session mappings in detail and add targeted reconciliation tooling (separate ticket).
